text:
ConocoPhillips gained 1.6% today, recovering some ground after a sharp 7.6% drop over the past two weeks. The bounce comes as crude oil prices have stabilized around $89–92 per barrel; the stock has climbed steadily for three days as oil recovered from earlier lows. The heating oil shortage story (prices up 59% year-over-year) underscores tight energy markets, which can support oil and integrated energy company valuations.

The longer context is pushback: Russia's crude production rebounded in October to 8.73 million barrels a day, and the IEA noted global oil supply has returned to surplus. That surplus condition likely explains why the stock fell 7.6% in the first place — more barrels on the market mean lower prices and margin pressure for producers. Today's rebound may simply reflect a pause in that downward momentum rather than a reversal of the supply glut concern.
